terms.grammar: adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis)
terms.comment: Janus’s month (Varro, LL 6.34, rightly). Like every Roman month name it is an adjective: mēnse Jānuāriō, or Jānuāriō alone, “in January”; Kalendae, Nōnae, Īdūs Jānuāriae, the 1st, 5th and 13th. Traupman gives the modern way of dating as well (p. 76).

phrases.latin: quā rē Jānuāriō mēnse, ut cōnstituistī, cūrā ut Rōmae sīs
phrases.english: so be sure to be in Rome in January, as you planned

phrases.latin: sed heus tū, diem meum scīs esse III Nōnās Jānuāriās; aderis igitur
phrases.english: but listen: you know my birthday is the third day before the Nones of January, the 3rd; so you’ll be there
On the third of January (the modern way; Traupman’s Cicero, giving his birthday).
